desc:
Approval workflow automation for requests turns expense, time-off and discount questions into a simple yes or no decision. Ecom Swift LLC builds approval flows that reach the right person, remind them politely and save every decision with a date.

## What is approval workflow automation?

Approval workflow automation is a set of rules that sends a request to the person who must decide, collects their answer, and tells the requester what happened. The request carries its own details, so the approver does not need to hunt through an email thread. The answer is one click, and the outcome is stored where you can find it later.

Typical requests include purchase and expense claims, time-off days, discount exceptions, content sign-off, refunds above a set amount and new supplier requests.

## Why approvals stall when they live in email

Most approvals begin as a message that says "can you OK this?" The approver is busy, the message sinks under newer mail, and the requester waits without knowing whether anyone has seen it. Someone eventually asks again, a second thread starts, and nobody is sure which reply counts.

The cost is not only delay. Staff cannot plan around an answer they do not have. Managers spend time answering the same questions about missing details. When an auditor, a partner or a boss asks who approved a payment and when, the evidence is scattered across inboxes. A clear flow removes each of these problems at the source.

## How a good flow changes day-to-day work

The main gain is speed with accountability. When the approver gets a message with the amount, the reason, the requester and two buttons, deciding takes seconds rather than a reply that needs thought about what is being asked. Reminders pull slow answers forward without anyone playing the nag.

The record helps too. Because each decision is saved with a name and a date, you can see which request types wait longest, which approvers are overloaded and where a rule is too strict or too loose. That evidence lets you adjust limits and cover for absences with facts instead of guesses.

## What a great approval flow includes

- A clear request form or trigger, so every request arrives with the same required details.
- Routing rules based on amount, department or request type.
- One-click approve and reject buttons inside the message the approver already reads.
- A comment field so a reason can be added to a decision.
- Reminders sent when an answer is slow.
- A backup approver who takes over when the main approver is away.
- A second level of approval for requests above a set limit.
- Automatic notice to the requester with the outcome.
- A saved log of requests, decisions, names and dates in a sheet you own.
- A short guide showing how to change an approver or a limit.

## What we do

We start by listing your request types and who currently decides each one. We write down the limits, the exceptions and what should happen when an approver is away. Then we build the flow in the tools you already use, such as your forms, email, Slack or Microsoft Teams, and a spreadsheet for the record.

The Basic package covers one request type with one approver. Standard adds several request types, routing by amount or department, reminders and a backup approver. Premium adds two-level approval above limits, a simple request form for staff, a periodic report of volumes and response times, and a guide for editing approvers. We test every route with sample requests before it touches real ones, and we show you how a rejected or abandoned request behaves.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide in advance who approves what, including who covers during absences.
- Keep the request form short and ask only for what the approver needs.
- Set limits that match how your business really spends.
- Make the outcome visible to the requester right away.
- Review the saved log now and then to see where requests wait.

**Avoid:**
- Sending every request to the owner by default.
- Adding extra approval levels for small, low-risk requests.
- Letting approvers decide through chat replies that the flow cannot record.
- Building one giant flow for every request type before testing a simple one.
- Hiding the rules, so staff guess who to ask.

## Who this is for

This suits a small agency whose owner approves every expense and is tired of chasing receipts in chat. It also suits a shop team that must get sign-off before giving a discount beyond a set level. A growing company with managers in different departments, where time-off and purchase requests currently pass through personal inboxes, will see the same gain.

## What we need from you

Tell us your request types, who decides each one, any limits and what the requester should be told. Share your current form or email example and say which tools your team uses. Access is given to us as a collaborator, staff or team user in your own accounts where the tool supports it, so you stay in control. We never need your passwords, and you can remove access when the work is done.
